definition: Discordant means not in harmony or agreement.
task: Write one sentence of your own using the word discordant. Make the sentence show what the word means -- a reader who did not know discordant should be able to work it out from your sentence.
avoid_verbatim: During warm-up, a single out-of-tune violin produced a discordant whine that cut through the orchestra's careful tuning.
Mismatched things merely fail to go together, while discordant things actively clash or grate against each other.
A discordant sound clashes with what surrounds it, but a cacophonous one is a full, deafening jumble of harsh noise.

Clashing is the everyday word for things that conflict sharply - clashing colors, clashing schedules - and it stays casual. Discordant is its more formal cousin, at home in writing about music, meetings, and ideas, and it always evokes a jarring failure of parts to harmonize with one another.

Jarring describes the effect on you: a jarring note or image gives an unpleasant jolt, striking you as harsh and out of place. Discordant describes the relationship between parts: elements that fail to harmonize with each other. A single scream is jarring; two melodies fighting each other are discordant.

Inharmonious is the neutral, technical way to say parts lack harmony, and it stops at flat description. Discordant is sharper: it says the parts actively grate against one another, the way an out-of-tune string cuts through an ensemble. Inharmonious notes merely fail to blend; discordant ones clash.

Discordant means not in harmony or agreement.
At the reunion, the conversation about where to hold next year's gathering quickly turned discordant.
Three aunts wanted the lake house, two cousins insisted on the city, and no two voices seemed to agree on anything.
The family's clashing, conflicting opinions show that discordant describes disagreement between people, not only harsh sound.
Discordant is an adjective; it describes a note, a color scheme, or a relationship that clashes.
Its related noun, dissonance, names the lack of harmony itself and is taught separately in this unit, so keep discordant for describing things: a discordant chord, a discordant meeting.

The library's new wing opened to strong opinions and a long letters column in the local paper.
The old building is warm brick and rounded arches; the addition is sheet steel, angled like a wedge into the original facade.
Supporters call the pairing bold.
Detractors call it discordant: two designs that grate against each other at every seam instead of talking to one another.
